name: Philippines insurgencies (NPA and Islamist militants in Mindanao)
started: 1969 (NPA communist insurgency; Islamist insurgencies in Mindanao long-running)
summary: The Philippines' communist and Islamist insurgencies are much weaker than a decade ago but still produce deadly encounters, such as the killing of 19 suspected NPA fighters on Negros in April 2026. In Muslim Mindanao, the long-delayed first Bangsamoro parliament election was finally held on 14 September 2026.

sides.name: New People's Army (NPA)
members: New People's Army (armed wing of the Communist Party of the Philippines)

sides.name: Dawlah Islamiyah-Maute Group
members: Dawlah Islamiyah-Maute Group (involved in the 2017 Marawi siege)

background: The NPA has fought the state since 1969 and the Bangsamoro region was created under a peace deal with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, but splinter Islamist groups such as the Dawlah Islamiyah-Maute Group, which helped lead the 2017 siege of Marawi, remain active in Lanao del Sur. The first election for the Bangsamoro Parliament was repeatedly postponed and was reset by Republic Act No. 12317 to the second Monday of September 2026. This matters because a credible regional government is the main bulwark against renewed Moro insurgency.
year: On 17 April 2026 a joint operation killed ten Dawlah Islamiyah-Maute members in Marantao, Lanao del Sur. On 19 April nineteen suspected NPA members were killed in encounters with the military in Toboso, Negros Occidental. On 21 August Marantao's vice mayor was arrested on murder charges. The Bangsamoro Parliament election took place on 14 September; the Bangsamoro Federalist Party won a plurality and the United Bangsamoro Justice Party won all six sectoral seats.
situation: As of late October 2026 both insurgencies are at a low ebb, with sporadic military operations. Attention in Mindanao has shifted to forming the first elected Bangsamoro government.
technical: 19 Apr 2026: 19 suspected NPA members killed in encounters with the military at Toboso, Negros Occidental (Wikipedia).
17 Apr 2026: 10 Dawlah Islamiyah-Maute members killed in a joint law enforcement operation in Marantao, Lanao del Sur (Wikipedia).
Bangsamoro Parliament election held 14 Sep 2026 under RA 12317; Bangsamoro Federalist Party plurality; UBJP won all six sectoral seats (Wikipedia).
No sourced 2026 NPA surrenders or Abu Sayyaf activity were found (Wikipedia).
casualties: At least 29 militants killed in the two April 2026 operations (Wikipedia: 2026 in the Philippines). No comprehensive 2026 total retrieved.

timeline.event: Ten Dawlah Islamiyah-Maute members killed in Marantao.
Nineteen suspected NPA members killed in Toboso, Negros Occidental.

outlook: Watch the formation of the new Bangsamoro government and whether losing factions or splinter groups turn to violence, and whether the NPA's remaining fronts on Negros and elsewhere are dismantled.

battles.outcome: Military reported 19 suspected NPA members killed.
battles.significance: The deadliest single NPA loss found for 2026, on one of the insurgency's last strong islands.

battles.outcome: Ten group members killed in a joint law enforcement operation.
battles.significance: Targeted remnants of the group behind the 2017 Marawi siege ahead of the Bangsamoro election.
